source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 14ης Μαΐου — «Άγιος Μάρκος ο Νεομάρτυρας ο Κρής που μαρτύρησε στη Σμύρνη»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 14 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. **He is none of the corpus's Marks** — of Byblos, of Ephesus, the Deaf, the Shepherd and the rest — which the namesweep flagged and which were read; a Cretan of the seventeenth century who apostatised for four years and returned answers to none of them. **The display name keeps «ο Κρής» and drops the place of martyrdom**, the epithet being what the Greek calendar tells him by. **Three men are named and none has a folder**: his father Andreas of Zakynthos, his teacher at Constantinople Meletios Syrigos, and the Jesuit Isaac I who wrote his martyrdom. **No `locations` object**, although Crete, Zakynthos, Smyrna, the Toplou monastery of Sitia and Constantinople are all named. No hymn is printed; the page says he was buried at the church of Saint Photini in Smyrna and became a spring of healings.
